title: חזקיה בנו של ר' חייא הגדול

paragraphs: Chizkiyah, son of R. Chiyya the Great, and his brother Yehudah (see there) were born from one drop that divided in two: Niddah 27a. Chizkiyah's form was completed three months before Yehudah's. Shalshelet HaKabbalah likewise writes this (32b). However, Yuchasin, letter yod, writes the reverse: Yehudah emerged three months earlier. The end of chapter 6 of Yevamot does not decide which was born first, for it says: “Yehudah and Chizkiyah were twins; one had his form completed at the end of nine months and the other at the beginning of seven.” I will judge and decide: since it puts Yehudah before Chizkiyah, it appears that Yehudah was born first. Further evidence: in the cave, Yehudah was buried to the right of his father R. Chiyya and Chizkiyah to his father's left, as in Moed Katan (see Rav Huna above); see that Yehudah was the older. They also had two twin sisters; see R. Chiyya above. At the beginning of Mi SheMetu (18b), R. Chiyya's sons went to the countryside—to attend to work on their estate, according to Rashi. They had forgotten their learning, and they were distressed trying to remember it. One said to the other, “Does our father know of this distress?” The other said, “How would he know? It is written, ‘His sons achieve honor and he does not know.’” The other said, “Does he not know? But it is written, ‘Only his flesh upon him suffers,’ and R. Yitzchak said: the worm is painful to the dead, etc.” He is called Berabbi; see there. “Chizkiyah said,” and likewise “the school of Chizkiyah taught”: Shabbat 24b, 133a. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 38b, writes that Chizkiyah and Bar Kappara are tannaim and older than R. Yehudah Nesia. He was R. Yochanan's teacher; see there. In Zevachim 56b and Chagigah 8a, 9a, Chizkiyah and R. Yochanan disagree. Shabbat 112b has “Rabbi Chizkiyah, etc.; R. Yochanan said to him: ‘My teacher, you taught us.’” The word “Rabbi” is a scribal error, since they were not ordained. Rashba, chapter HaMegaresh (84), writes that there were two Chizkiyahs: one was R. Yochanan's teacher, and the other was Chizkiyah son of R. Chiyya son of Rav Kahana, a Babylonian. The law follows R. Yochanan even though Chizkiyah disagrees, because this is not his teacher but Chizkiyah son of R. Chiyya son of Rav Kahana: Sefer Techillat Chokhmah, folio 51, column 4. See HaMegaresh 84b, where R. Yochanan disagrees with Chizkiyah. Rashba writes concerning this that this Chizkiyah was not his teacher. Accordingly, one may explain, as Rashi seems to imply, that R. Yochanan said to Chizkiyah, “Your man said”—meaning Rav Kahana. The Chizkiyah to whom R. Yochanan said “Your man said” was not his teacher, but the second Chizkiyah, son of R. Chiyya son of Rav Kahana. One thus need not explain, as Tosafot does, that R. Yochanan said “Your man said” to his students from Babylonia. Understand this. Yet I have not found in the Talmud a Chizkiyah son of Rav Chiyya son of Rav Kahana. If it is a received tradition, we will accept it. Rif, chapter Ein Maamidin, writes that the law follows Chizkiyah even though R. Yochanan disagrees, since the law does not follow a student against his teacher. The work abbreviated N״Ch, Yoreh Deah, section 145, writes: “We hold like Chizkiyah against R. Yochanan, since he was his teacher. Yavin Shemuah writes that this means in his presence, etc. If so, who says that R. Yochanan was in his presence?” End of quotation.
